items.name: Eigenvector and eigenvalue
items.when: To test a vector: multiply it by $A$ and see whether you get a multiple of it. The multiple is $\lambda$.
items.cue: The equation that makes a non-zero $v$ an eigenvector of $A$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$

items.name: Multiples of an eigenvector
items.when: An eigenvector is a whole line through the origin. Any non-zero multiple, negative ones too, has the same $\lambda$.
items.cue: What $A$ does to $cv$ when $v$ is an eigenvector for $\lambda$

items.name: Collect v on one side
items.when: $Av = \lambda v$ rewritten as one matrix times $v$. $A - \lambda I$ is $A$ with $\lambda$ taken off the diagonal only.
items.cue: $Av = \lambda v$ rewritten as a single matrix times $v$

items.name: The eigenvalue equation
items.when: To find every eigenvalue without guessing vectors: a non-zero $v$ is sent to 0 exactly when the determinant is 0.
items.cue: The equation in $\lambda$ alone whose roots are the eigenvalues of $A$

items.name: Trace and determinant
items.when: The two numbers the $2 \times 2$ shortcut needs. The trace is the diagonal only; $bc$ is subtracted.
items.cue: The trace and the determinant of a $2 \times 2$ matrix, from its four entries

items.name: The 2×2 shortcut
items.when: To write $\det(A - \lambda I)$ for a $2 \times 2$ at once, from the trace and the determinant.
items.cue: The characteristic polynomial of a $2 \times 2$ matrix in terms of its trace and determinant

items.name: Sum and product of eigenvalues
items.when: To check eigenvalues you found, or to guess them when they are integers.
items.cue: What the two eigenvalues of a $2 \times 2$ add up to and multiply to

items.name: Eigenvector from an eigenvalue
items.formula: Solve $(A - \lambda I)\,v = 0$: both rows give one equation; pick $x = 1$.
items.when: Once you have $\lambda$. If the two rows do not say the same thing, $\lambda$ or $A - \lambda I$ has a slip.
items.cue: How to get the eigenvector for a known eigenvalue $\lambda$ of a $2 \times 2$

items.name: Check by multiplying
items.when: Always multiply back: if $Bv$ is not $\lambda v$, something earlier went wrong.
items.cue: In the course's example $B = \begin{bmatrix}4&1\\2&3\end{bmatrix}$: the check that $(1, -2)$ is an eigenvector for 2

items.name: Symmetric means perpendicular
items.formula: $S^\mathsf{T} = S$: eigenvectors for different eigenvalues are perpendicular.
items.when: For any symmetric matrix, including every $A^\mathsf{T}A$. A non-symmetric one, like $B$, need not have them.
items.cue: What is true of the eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix, for two different eigenvalues

items.name: Singular values
items.when: To get the stretches of $A$ in its SVD, largest first. Do not stop at $\lambda$: take the root.
items.cue: How each singular value $\sigma_i$ of $A$ comes from an eigenvalue

items.name: Right singular vectors
items.when: To get the input directions of the SVD. Scale each eigenvector to length 1.
items.cue: Where the right singular vectors $v_i$ of $A$ come from, and how long $A v_i$ is
